title: Identity connector resilience and graceful user eviction (SCIM provisioning reliability)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers have reported sporadic orphaned accounts after SCIM deprovision waves from large IdPs. Root causes include partial failure during multi-resource writes (user + group links), non-idempotent retry semantics between our SCIM worker and third-party IdP rate limits, and insufficient audit metadata to reconcile post-failure. This ticket implements connector-level resilience and a graceful user-eviction flow that guarantees eventual consistency without unintended deletions.
goals: 1) Ensure SCIM provisioning operations (create/update/delete) are idempotent across retries. 2) Implement a quarantine/eviction window for deletion requests so we can recover from partial failures. 3) Add observability and audit enrichment for each provisioning attempt to support postmortems and customer reconciliation. 4) Provide a safe rollout path with feature flag and migration backfill.
acceptance_criteria:
- SCIM delete requests are recorded with an eviction_token and a scheduled eviction timestamp.
- Retries use idempotency keys; duplicate inbound events do not create inconsistent state.
- Quarantine window default is 24 hours (configurable per-org); during this window the user is marked "pending_deletion" in our system and remains queryable for admins.
- A backfill job can reconcile pending_deletion users older than X days and either finalize deletion or re-queue (configurable).
- Audit logs include operation_id, idempotency_key, connector_version, outbound HTTP status, and response body hash.
- E2E tests cover transient 429/5xx errors, long-poll retry paths, and graceful rollbacks if deletion finalizes prematurely.
technical_decisions:
- Use a per-operation idempotency_key derived from (org_id, scim_event_id, resource_type, timestamp_bucket) to avoid collisions across rapid duplicate events.
- Introduce a new user state 'pending_deletion' instead of immediate tombstone; final deletion is executed by a controlled worker after quarantine.
- Implement exponential jittered backoff with explicit rate-limit-aware cooldown when SCIM partners return 429 or Retry-After.
- Store last_provision_attempt metadata on the user row (timestamp, operation_id, attempt_count, response_code) to aid reconcilers.
- Audit log format extended to include response_body_sha256 to enable deterministic equality checks without storing payloads.
- Default quarantine window set to 24h with org-level override via private setting.
- Provide a safety gate in the worker: if >10% of pending_deletion for an org are older than 72h, create an alert and pause automated finalization until manual review.
tradeoffs:
- Keeping users in pending_deletion increases storage and complexity for short-lived deletions but dramatically reduces accidental permanent data loss.
- Idempotency keys add complexity when customers perform rapid resyncs from different IdPs; we mitigate by including scim_event_id and timestamp bucket.
- Quarantine introduces a delay to actual deletions which some customers might dislike; we expose org-level setting to tune down to 0 for advanced customers with strong guarantees.
implementation_plan:
1) Schema migration: add fields (pending_deletion_at, eviction_token, last_provision_attempt, idempotency_key_history) with careful online migration.
2) Connector changes: emit idempotency_key on outbound requests, interpret Retry-After and response codes to drive backoff.
3) Worker changes: implement quarantine scheduling, safe finalizer with safety gate and metrics.
4) Observability: add metrics (scim.ops.total, scim.ops.retries, scim.deletion.quarantine_count, scim.finalize_errors) and tracing tags.
5) Audit: extend audit sink and retention rules, add response_body_sha256.
6) Tests: unit, integration against a mocked IdP that simulates 429, 500 and partial success.
7) Backfill: implement a migration job that converts recently deleted users to pending_deletion with eviction_token.
8) Rollout behind feature flag + canary orgs for 48-72h before wide rollout.
rollout_plan:
- Canary: enable feature for 3 internal and 5 small customer orgs for 72h, monitor SLOs and reconciliation dashboards.
- Stage: enable for 10% of production orgs for 7 days.
- Gradual: ramp to 100% over 2 weeks if no critical regressions.
- Emergency kill: feature flag to revert to existing immediate deletion flow.
- Communication: runbook for CS and Support including how to restore a quarantined user and how to finalize deletion manually.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for idempotency key generation and history TTL.
- Integration tests with simulated IdP that returns 429 (with Retry-After), 500, partial successes (200 + 207 multi-status).
- Load test: simulate a burst of 20k deprovision events across 1,200 orgs to validate queue/backpressure behavior.
- Chaos test: randomly drop outbound HTTP responses to ensure reconciler can recover.
- Post-deploy: run a reconciliation run comparing audit logs -> DB state for canary orgs.
